9-panel cinematic storyboard sheet derived from Image 1. Mix Wide, Medium, and Tight shots of the same scene. No borders between panels.

Layout: 3x3 grid (9 panels) in a 16:9 landscape image.

Scene: Cinematic 16:9 editorial beauty-campaign still, handheld low-angle framing, gritty tactile realism. SCARLETT VEGA (Image 2) wears a fitted black cotton turtleneck with sleeves pushed up to her elbows, dark slim jeans, scuffed black ankle boots, and a slouchy dark denim-canvas jacket, a heavy natural-canvas tote bag slung over one shoulder, small gold hoop earrings and a thin silver ring on her right index finger. She stands mid-stride in a tight basement club back corridor, having just pulled the lipstick tube from her jacket pocket — she holds the product from (CORAL_LIPSTICK (Image 4)) low in her right hand, capped, angled slightly toward the lens and catching a hard specular kick of red light, giving it one dismissive downward glance with a deadpan raised eyebrow, no intention of reapplying, while her left forearm is already lifting to shove the heavy black stage curtain aside, the fabric beginning to swing and billow in a slow dark arc at the end of the passage. The corridor is exposed painted brick plastered with layers of peeling old flyers and taped set lists, black-painted pipes and conduit crowding the low ceiling just above her head, scuffed concrete floor gritty with dust and gaffer-tape scars, a scratched fire door and a stacked road case shoved against the wall in the background. A single red EXIT fixture just out of frame is the key, spilling crimson across the bricks with deep rapid falloff into near-black, a dirty amber bulb bleeding faintly from a doorway beyond, hot rim light along the ridge of her jacket shoulder and a crimson highlight on the tube's glossy surface. Shot low and close on a 28mm lens, slight upward tilt, natural handheld micro-shake, shallow depth of field with the curtain edge softening into bokeh, punchy contrast, crisp true-to-life skin warmth against the saturated red-and-black palette, fine 35mm grain.

Every panel is a shot of the same scene as Image 1 — keep the characters, wardrobe, lighting, color grade, and texture consistent across all panels.

No text, dialogue bubbles, scene numbers, or watermarks.

Reference images define identity — keep every referenced character, object, and location consistent with its reference image; never render a reference image itself as a separate panel or subject.
